messages:
sam-support: Hi team — running into an import error after installing the Python SDK with extras. pip install -e .[fastapi] from my local checkout, then in a fresh venv `from redwood import Client` raises ImportError: cannot import name 'Client' from 'redwood' (unknown location). Anyone seen this?

ingrid-support: thanks for the report — quick Qs: which package name did you install (pip output), python version, and can you paste `python -c 'import redwood, inspect, sys; print(redwood.__file__); print(sys.path[:3])'`?

sam-support: python 3.11.4, poetry/venv. pip freeze shows: 
```
-e git+file:///Users/sam/dev/redwood-sdk@main#egg=redwood
fastapi==0.95.2
uvicorn==0.22.0
httpx==0.24.1
```
And the import probe prints: 
```
/Users/sam/dev/redwood-sdk/redwood/__init__.py
['', '/Users/sam/.pyenv/versions/3.11.4/lib/python3.11/site-packages', ...]
```
So looks like it's importing the local checkout rather than the installed SDK wheel. I installed editable to develop, but then added extras.

matt-devx: ah — two likely issues people trip over: 1) editable installs don't copy extras into your local package dir, they create an egg-link that points to source; `pip install -e .[fastapi]` should, in theory, install extras, but if you later run `python -m pip install .` or have a local folder named `redwood` in your CWD it can shadow. 2) if your repo layout isn't a proper package (pkg name mismatch) the import path can be confusing.

sam-support: repo layout is `redwood/` top-level package (with __init__.py), setup.cfg/pyproject.toml defines name = "redwood-sdk". Could that mismatch cause the import to bind to local dir but missing runtime glue (Client class defined only in installed package path)?

ingrid-support: yes — if the distribution name (what pip knows) is different from the import package name, editable installs point to your local package code. If you were expecting the packaged wheel's built artifacts (generated during sdist/wheel build) you won't get them in editable mode. Also extras install additional deps (fastapi, etc.) but they don't inject code into your package. Can you `grep` for Client definition in your local tree: `rg "class Client"`?

sam-support: ran `rg "class Client" .` in repo: nothing. In the installed egg-link site-packages there is an egg-info that references the repo path. So looks like the public SDK exposes `redwood` as the top-level package and Client lives in `redwood.client` when installed from PyPI, but our local checkout is an older skeleton that doesn't export Client at package top-level. I forked earlier and haven't pulled latest changes.

matt-devx: that lines up — editable install is using your stale local code which doesn't have Client. Two pragmatic options: 1) uninstall the editable install (`pip uninstall redwood`) and `pip install redwood==<release>` so you get the published wheel which has Client, or 2) update your local checkout to match upstream (pull main) and run tests locally. For reproducing support issues it's helpful to test in a clean env: `python -m venv /tmp/rtest && source /tmp/rtest/bin/activate && pip install redwood[fastapi]` — that should match what customers see.

sam-support: tried option 1: after `pip uninstall redwood` the import error changed to ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'uvicorn' — oh, extras weren't installed by default because I did bare `pip install redwood`.

ingrid-support: yep extras must be explicit: `pip install 'redwood[fastapi]'` or `pip install redwood[all]` depending on names. Some packaging tools also require quoting to avoid shell expansion.

sam-support: interesting edge-case: earlier I had `pip install -e .` which created egg-link and then later even after uninstalling, the `redwood` name still resolved to my repo path (egg-link persisted?) I had to rm the *.egg-link in site-packages and `pip cache purge` to clean it. fwiw.

matt-devx: good note — editable egg-links are just files in site-packages, uninstall should remove them but if you switched venvs things can get messy. For future: avoid `-e` when reproducing user installs; build a wheel: `python -m build` then `pip install dist/redwood-*.whl` so you test the packaged artifact.

sam-support: thanks — one more odd thing: after installing published wheel, imports worked but runtime fails with `TypeError: AsyncClient.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'timeout'` — looks like httpx major version mismatch from our app's lockfile. The wheel requires httpx>=0.23 but my app had locked 0.20 via transitive dep.

ingrid-support: that's a classic dependency conflict. Two ways to mitigate: 1) update your lockfile to allow the newer httpx or 2) use an isolated env for the service or use constraint files to ensure compatibility. We also add a runtime guard in the SDK to raise clearer error if httpx is <minimum. I'll file a quick issue for the SDK to validate httpx version at import time.

matt-devx: summarizing action items: sam — reproduce in clean venv and attach `pip list` and `python -c 'import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)'` if still failing; prefer wheel installs when verifying extras. Ingrid — open an SDK issue to check httpx version on import and improve install docs about editable vs wheel + extras.

sam-support: done — repro worked with wheel and `pip install 'redwood[fastapi]'`, and fixed by bumping httpx in my app. Thanks all :thumbsup:
